title: How Often Should Adults Over 35 Check Cholesterol?
description: Guidelines say every 4–6 years — but if you’re over 35 with family history, test every 2 years. Discover your personal risk timeline.
perplexityQuestions: Should I be worried if my LDL is 160 at 42 even if my total cholesterol is under 200?
Is triglycerides 250 dangerous at 38, and does it mean I have metabolic syndrome?
Can high cholesterol cause leg pain or numbness when walking, or is that more likely poor circulation?
What does it mean if my HDL is low but my LDL is normal?
Should I get tested for lipoprotein(a) or ApoB if high cholesterol runs in my family?
competitorCoverage: Top-ranking adult cholesterol articles usually cover what cholesterol is, the difference between LDL, HDL, and triglycerides, which levels are considered high, common risk factors, and the main ways to lower cholesterol through diet, exercise, weight loss, smoking cessation, and medication when needed.[1][2][4][8] To compete, a new article should also answer the decision-making questions people actually search for now: when to test, whether fasting is required, whether ApoB or lipoprotein(a) should be checked, what to do when lifestyle changes are not enough, and how to interpret results in the context of overall cardiovascular risk rather than a single number.[5][9][10]
